sections.title: 1. About this manual
sections.text: This manual covers the HX-500 vertical machining center built from serial number HX5-2201 onwards (Rev C controller, firmware 4.x). Machines with serial numbers up to HX5-2200 use the Rev B controller; where Rev B behaves differently it is stated in a "Rev B note". Read chapter 2 (Safety) before operating the machine. Only operators who have completed the Level 1 HX-500 training may run programs; only Level 2 technicians may perform the tasks marked (L2).
sections.summary: This manual covers the HX 500 vertical machining center built from serial number HX5 2201 onwards (Rev C controller, firmware 4.x).

sections.title: 2.1 General safety rules
sections.text: Never open the enclosure door while the spindle is turning. The door interlock stops the spindle within 2 seconds; do not bypass it. Wear safety glasses at all times in the machining area. Gloves must not be worn while the spindle is running. Long hair must be tied back and loose clothing secured. Keep the floor area within 1 meter of the machine free of chips and coolant.
sections.summary: Never open the enclosure door while the spindle is turning.

sections.title: 2.2 Emergency stop
sections.text: Press the red EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator panel or on the side of the enclosure. All axes and the spindle stop and hydraulic pressure is released. To restart: remove the cause, twist the button to release it, press RESET, then re-home all axes (HOME ALL).
sections.summary: Press the red EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator panel or on the side of the enclosure.

sections.title: 2.3 Lockout / tagout
sections.text: Before any maintenance task marked (L2), and before opening the electrical cabinet, apply lockout/tagout as described in the Plant Safety Standard, section 4. Switch off the main isolator, lock it with your personal padlock, and wait 5 minutes for the spindle drive capacitors to discharge.
sections.summary: Before any maintenance task marked (L2), and before opening the electrical cabinet, apply lockout/tagout as described in the Plant Safety Standard, section 4.

sections.title: 4.1 Foundation
sections.text: The machine must stand on a reinforced concrete floor at least 200 mm thick. Level the machine to within 0.02 mm/m using the six leveling bolts. Re-check the level after the first month of operation and then every 6 months.
sections.summary: The machine must stand on a reinforced concrete floor at least 200 mm thick.

sections.title: 4.2 Environment
sections.text: Ambient temperature 10 - 35 °C, relative humidity below 75 % (non-condensing). For accuracy work (tolerances below 0.01 mm) the room temperature must be held within +/- 1 °C of 20 °C.
sections.summary: Ambient temperature 10 35 °C, relative humidity below 75 % (non condensing).

sections.title: 4.3 Electrical connection
sections.text: The machine must be connected by a qualified electrician to a dedicated circuit protected by a 63 A slow-blow fuse. The protective earth resistance must not exceed 0.1 ohm.
sections.summary: The machine must be connected by a qualified electrician to a dedicated circuit protected by a 63 A slow blow fuse.

sections.title: 5.1 Daily start-up
sections.text: 1. Check the air pressure gauge: 6 - 8 bar. 2. Check the way-lube oil level (sight glass at least half full). 3. Check the coolant level and concentration (see 7.4). 4. Switch on the main isolator and wait for the controller to boot (about 90 seconds). 5. Release the emergency stop and press RESET. 6. Press HOME ALL to home the axes. 7. Run the spindle warm-up program (see 5.2).

sections.title: 5.2 Spindle warm-up
sections.text: Run program O9000 (warm-up) whenever the spindle has been stopped for more than 4 hours, and always at the start of each shift. The program runs the spindle for 5 minutes at 1,000 rpm, 5 minutes at 4,000 rpm and 5 minutes at 8,000 rpm (15 minutes total). If the machine has been stopped for more than 72 hours, use the extended program O9001 instead (30 minutes, up to 12,000 rpm). Rev B note: on Rev B machines the extended program is O9002 and runs up to 10,000 rpm.
sections.summary: Run program O9000 (warm up) whenever the spindle has been stopped for more than 4 hours, and always at the start of each shift.

sections.title: 5.3 Loading tools
sections.text: Tools are loaded at the tool-change station with the spindle stopped. Each tool must be measured on the presetter and its length and diameter entered in the tool table before use. Tools heavier than 7 kg or longer than 300 mm must not be loaded. Adjacent pockets must be left empty for tools with a diameter above 80 mm (maximum 125 mm with empty adjacent pockets).
sections.summary: Tools are loaded at the tool change station with the spindle stopped.

sections.title: 5.4 Running a program
sections.text: Select the program, run it first in DRY RUN mode with the feed override at 25 % and single block on, then run the first part with the rapid override at 25 %. Only after the first part has been measured and approved may the program run in automatic mode at 100 % override.
sections.summary: Select the program, run it first in DRY RUN mode with the feed override at 25 % and single block on, then run the first part with the rapid override at 25 %.

sections.title: 5.5 Shutdown
sections.text: At the end of the last shift: remove chips from the table, park the axes with program O9010, switch the coolant pump off, and switch off the main isolator. Do not switch off the main isolator while an alarm is active; record the alarm number first.
sections.summary: At the end of the last shift: remove chips from the table, park the axes with program O9010, switch the coolant pump off, and switch off the main isolator.

sections.title: 6.1 Clearing a tool change timeout (A206)
sections.text: 1. Press RESET. 2. Switch to MDI mode and run M190 (tool changer recovery). 3. Check that the tool number on the screen matches the tool in the spindle. 4. If A206 occurs again within the same shift, stop and call a Level 2 technician.

sections.title: 6.2 Spindle over-temperature (A302)
sections.text: Stop the cycle and let the spindle idle with the chiller running for 30 minutes. Check that the chiller filter is clean and the chiller tank is above the MIN mark. Do not restart production until the spindle temperature is below 45 °C. If A302 occurs twice in one week, a Level 2 technician must check the spindle bearings.
sections.summary: Stop the cycle and let the spindle idle with the chiller running for 30 minutes.

sections.title: 7.3 Drawbar force check (L2)
sections.text: The drawbar clamping force must be between 12 and 14 kN for BT40 tools. Measure with the drawbar force gauge. If the force is below 12 kN, replace the disc spring stack. Never run the machine with a clamping force below 10 kN.
sections.summary: The drawbar clamping force must be between 12 and 14 kN for BT40 tools.

sections.title: 7.4 Coolant
sections.text: Use water-miscible coolant at 6 - 8 % concentration (refractometer reading x 1.0 for Helix Cool 300). Below 5 % there is a risk of corrosion and bacterial growth; above 10 % the coolant foams and can irritate the skin. Check the concentration daily and the pH weekly (target pH 8.5 - 9.5).
sections.summary: Use water miscible coolant at 6 8 % concentration (refractometer reading x 1.0 for Helix Cool 300).

sections.title: 7.5 Ballscrew backlash (L2)
sections.text: Measure the backlash on each axis with a dial indicator. The limit is 0.010 mm. Between 0.010 and 0.020 mm, enter backlash compensation in parameter group 1850. Above 0.020 mm the ballscrew must be replaced.
sections.summary: Measure the backlash on each axis with a dial indicator.

sections.title: 9. Warranty
sections.text: The machine is covered for 24 months from installation or 6,000 spindle hours, whichever comes first. The warranty does not cover damage from crashes, use of non-approved coolant, or maintenance not carried out according to chapter 7. Spindle bearings are covered for 12 months only if the warm-up rules in 5.2 have been followed (the controller logs warm-up runs).
sections.summary: The machine is covered for 24 months from installation or 6,000 spindle hours, whichever comes first.

sections.text: This service manual covers the HX-900 horizontal machining center. It is for Level 1 and Level 2 technicians.

sections.title: 1. Axis Drive maintenance
sections.text: A loose hose on the axis drive causes vibration and must be lubricateed within 25 hours. Use only Helix-approved brackets on the axis drive; others void the service agreement. A loose belt on the axis drive causes vibration and must be adjusted within 29 hours.
sections.summary: A loose hose on the axis drive causes vibration and must be lubricateed within 25 hours.

sections.title: 1.1 Adjust the axis drive coupling
sections.text: After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 23 seconds). The axis drive bearing must be adjusted by a Level 2 technician only. If the axis drive shows wear above 60 %, adjust the bearing before the next shift. A loose switch on the axis drive causes vibration and must be verifyed within 35 hours. If the axis drive shows wear above 10 %, clean the fuse before the next shift.
sections.summary: After any work on the axis drive, run the self test from the maintenance menu (about 23 seconds).

sections.title: 1.2 Inspect the axis drive coupling
sections.text: If the axis drive shows wear above 10 %, inspect the relay before the next shift. If the axis drive shows wear above 60 %, record the coupling before the next shift. After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 7 seconds). The axis drive cable must be checked by a Level 1 technician only. If the axis drive shows wear above 20 %, adjust the bracket before the next shift.
sections.summary: If the axis drive shows wear above 10 %, inspect the relay before the next shift.

sections.title: 1.3 Inspect the axis drive hose
sections.text: After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 46 seconds). The axis drive gasket must be recorded by a Level 1 technician only. Use only Helix-approved bearings on the axis drive; others void the service agreement. Every 800 hours, replace the axis drive coupling and note the result in the machine log. Every 1300 hours, verify the axis drive bearing and note the result in the machine log.
sections.summary: After any work on the axis drive, run the self test from the maintenance menu (about 46 seconds).

sections.title: 1.4 Inspect the axis drive sensor
sections.text: After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 46 seconds). A loose fuse on the axis drive causes vibration and must be checked within 22 hours. If the axis drive shows wear above 20 %, record the fuse before the next shift. Every 900 hours, tighten the axis drive valve and note the result in the machine log. sections.summary: After any work on the axis drive, run the self test from the maintenance menu (about 46 seconds).

sections.title: 1.5 Inspect the axis drive bearing
sections.text: A loose nozzle on the axis drive causes vibration and must be replaceed within 6 hours. A loose valve on the axis drive causes vibration and must be cleaned within 6 hours. Every 1750 hours, lubricate the axis drive nozzle and note the result in the machine log. If the axis drive shows wear above 10 %, lubricate the gasket before the next shift. After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 6 seconds).

sections.title: 1.6 Check the axis drive belt
sections.text: Every 100 hours, record the axis drive sensor and note the result in the machine log. After any work on the axis drive, run the self-test from the maintenance menu (about 11 seconds). The axis drive belt must be cleaned by a Level 2 technician only. If the axis drive shows wear above 30 %, measure the coupling before the next shift. Use only Helix-approved fuses on the axis drive; others void the service agreement.

sections.title: 1. Accounts and passwords
sections.text: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must not contain the user name. Passwords for normal accounts expire every 180 days; passwords for administrator accounts every 90 days. The last 10 passwords cannot be reused. After 5 failed sign-in attempts the account is locked for 30 minutes. The IT service desk can unlock it earlier after verifying the user's identity by a call-back to the registered mobile number. Shared accounts are not allowed, except machine-controller accounts on the shop floor, which are managed by the controls team.
sections.summary: Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and must not contain the user name.

sections.title: 2. Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
sections.text: MFA is required for email, VPN, the ERP system and every administrator account. Authenticator app codes are preferred; SMS codes are allowed only for employees without a company smartphone. Hardware security keys are mandatory for domain administrators.
sections.summary: MFA is required for email, VPN, the ERP system and every administrator account.

sections.title: 3. Remote access
sections.text: Remote access is only through the company VPN from a company laptop. Personal devices may access email and Teams through the mobile app with MFA, but may not connect to the VPN. Remote access to shop-floor machine controllers is not allowed, except for Helix service engineers through the vendor access gateway, with a work order and the approval of the plant controls engineer for each session.
sections.summary: Remote access is only through the company VPN from a company laptop.

sections.title: 4. USB and removable media
sections.text: USB storage devices are blocked on all office computers. On the shop floor, CNC programs are transferred through the DNC server; USB sticks may only be used on machines without a network connection (list kept by the controls team), and only sticks issued by IT, which are scanned at the kiosk before each use.
sections.summary: USB storage devices are blocked on all office computers.

sections.title: 5. Software
sections.text: Only software from the company software center may be installed. Requests for other software go through the IT service desk and need the approval of the information security officer (ISO). Freeware and browser extensions are treated the same way.
sections.summary: Only software from the company software center may be installed.

sections.title: 7. Incidents
sections.text: Report suspected phishing with the "Report phishing" button in Outlook. Report a lost or stolen laptop or phone to the IT service desk within 2 hours, and to the police within 24 hours if stolen. Security incidents involving personal data must be escalated to the data protection officer within 24 hours.
sections.summary: Report suspected phishing with the "Report phishing" button in Outlook.

sections.title: 8. Exceptions
sections.text: Exceptions to this standard need a written risk assessment and the approval of the chief information security officer (CISO). Exceptions are valid for at most 6 months and must be reviewed before they are renewed.
sections.summary: Exceptions to this standard need a written risk assessment and the approval of the chief information security officer (CISO).

sections.title: 2.2 Visitors

sections.title: 2.3 Contractors
sections.text: Contractors must complete the safety induction (45 minutes) before starting work and receive a contractor badge valid for 12 months. Contractors working at height or on electrical equipment also need a work permit (section 5) for each job.

sections.title: 4. Lockout / tagout (LOTO)
sections.text: 1. Inform the area supervisor and the machine operators. 2. Switch off the equipment using the normal stop. 3. Isolate all energy sources: electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, stored mechanical energy. 4. Apply your personal padlock and tag to every isolation point. Every person working on the equipment applies their own lock. 5. Release stored energy and wait the discharge time stated in the machine manual. 6. Verify zero energy: try to start the machine and measure voltage. 7. After the work, remove only your own lock. A lock left by someone who has left the site may only be removed by the area manager after a documented check, with the EHS head informed.

sections.title: 5. Work permits
sections.text: A work permit signed by the area supervisor and EHS is required for: hot work (welding, grinding, cutting outside the grinding bay), work at height above 1.8 meters, confined space entry, and electrical work on live equipment. Permits are valid for one shift. Hot work requires a fire watch for 30 minutes after the work ends. Electrical work on live equipment above 50 V additionally needs the approval of the plant electrical engineer.

sections.text: Only employees holding a valid Helix forklift license (renewed every 3 years) may drive forklifts. Speed limit 10 km/h in the warehouse and 5 km/h in production halls. Pedestrians have priority on marked walkways. Contractors may not drive Helix forklifts.

sections.title: 7. Working hours and fatigue
sections.text: No one may work more than 12 hours in a shift or more than 60 hours in a week, including overtime. Between two shifts there must be a rest period of at least 11 hours. Exceptions need the written approval of the plant manager and may not be used for more than 2 consecutive weeks.
